doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Her first songs: 'All the Pretty Bubbles' and an angry song in 1971
summary: She wrote a song about bubbles at four; her first real song came in 1971 from anger at her second husband.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No, I won’t. The other night you played a song, you said it was the first song you ever wrote, except the one about bubbles —
Right. I don’t usually mention that one. I was four.
What was the name of that song you wrote when you were four?

No not at all. But it was very interesting. It was very interesting structure. It went [sings] all the pretty bubbles I see/ all the pretty bubbles I see/all the pretty bubbles I see — and you know it kept going up, like the bubbles.
So I wasn’t quite separating music from other reality. I was a kid.
But the one then you said you wrote first, I thought was a pretty sophisticated song for the first one. But you said you didn’t write really until well into your career.

No. I guess I wrote that in ’71 and I started my first paying gig was in ’62. But you know there’s so many great songs out there that I would much rather take those songs and learn from them and make them my own, and you know, why would I want to write songs when there are such great songs out there, you know, “Please Send Me Someone to Love” or “It Hurts Me Too” or all these great songs. But I got so angry in 1971. I didn’t have any way to communicate. I couldn’t communicate except I just wrote a song, and it helped.
Was it — it turned out to be an angry song?
It was a very angry song. I’m going to cough now

It was a very angry song. It was — I was 26 years old and I was getting rid of the second husband at that point. I was always a little bit ahead of myself. And very happy to be getting rid of him and angry because he, you know, I was needing to get rid of him. So it really helped. The second song I wrote, which was right after, was about this new guy I’d met, who was also a problem. But he mellowed out. We’ve been together since 1971.
